title: Zone of Possible Agreement (ZOPA)
description: The invisible range between the seller's walk-away minimum and the buyer's walk-away maximum. Outside this zone, no deal is possible.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: The invisible range between the seller's walk-away minimum and the buyer's walk-away maximum. Outside this zone, no deal is possible.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: A vendor's absolute minimum is $40,000. Your maximum budget is $45,000. The ZOPA is $40,000–$45,000. Any settlement inside that range is better than no deal for both.
If your max is $38,000, there is no ZOPA. Pushing further wastes time and goodwill.

sections.title: Warning Signs of No ZOPA
content: One party's concessions are tiny fractions.
Phrases like 'That's just not feasible for us' repeated three times with no alternative solutions.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Before negotiating, estimate the other side's walk-away point by asking indirect questions: 'What other options would you consider?' or 'What does your fallback look like?'

sections.title: Common Mistake
sections.content: Assuming that because you want a deal badly, a ZOPA must exist. Wishing does not create one.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Know the boundaries of possible agreement before you fight over the space inside them.
